advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that creates a supersedes/duplicates link to a target that is deleted/archived (not live) in a readable tracker, and assert the gate refuses (verdict != 'disposition'), so the dead-target boundary is covered rather than only the unreadable-tracker fail-closed path.
evidence: docstring: "A link whose target is not a live ticket is not evidence."
test body creates no link (tid = _make(store, "story", "links a ghost")) and passes tracker=str(store / "no-such-tracker")

close_precheck._is_live_ticket / _has_live_replacement_link (close_precheck.py:91-108) walk deps and inbound links and check _is_live_ticket on the target; the discriminating case is a link present whose target is not live

_recorded_replacement_target docstring (close_precheck.py:111-118): the predicate and the recorded-target check differ in exactly one case -- 'a link exists but its target is archived, deleted, or no longer resolvable' -- which this test never constructs
advisory.finding: The 'retired replacement link' boundary is untested: test_superseded_naming_a_retired_replacement_is_still_refused constructs no link and points tracker at a nonexistent directory, so it exercises the fail-closed-on-unreadable-tracker branch rather than the 'link exists but its target is not a live ticket' path the docstring claims. A regression that treated a link with a dead/archived target as live evidence would not be caught.
scenarios: A future change causes _is_live_ticket to be skipped/short-circuited so any recorded supersedes link (even to a deleted target) grants the exemption; this test still passes because it only ever hits the unreadable-tracker except branch.
advisory.suggested_fix: Seed a real link to a target ticket, then delete/archive that target (or use a target id that resolves as not-live) in a readable tracker, and assert check['ok'] is False and verdict != 'disposition'. Keep the current no-such-tracker case as a separate explicit fail-closed test.
